parsedVerdict.reasoning:
An application-layer service should coordinate use cases: load aggregates, call domain behaviour, save through an abstraction. CoursesService does more than that, in two ways.

1. It holds a domain rule. `create` checks that capacity is between 1 and 300 inline and throws a DomainError. That is a rule the Course domain model should own and enforce, not something to set in a use-case method. `publish` likewise sets `entity.published = true` on the ORM record instead of calling domain behaviour on Course.

2. It does infrastructure work. It builds TypeORM queries directly (`findOne({ where: { id } })`, `find({ where: { published: true } })`, `create`/`save` on `Repository<CourseEntity>`). It also exports `toCourse`, which converts the persistence `CourseEntity` into the domain `Course`. That conversion belongs in a repository or adapter in the infrastructure layer.

Calling a repository from a NestJS service is a common, partly accepted pattern, which is why confidence is moderate. Even so, the inline invariant and the ORM-to-domain mapper are responsibilities of other layer kinds.
